annotation.authors_or_issuer: Mandl, S.; Bretschneider, M.; Meyer, S.; Gesmann-Nuissl, D.; Asbrock, F.; Meyer, B.; et al.
key_provisions_or_claims: Competence and Morality attributions to prosthesis users vary with technical sophistication of the prosthesis.
Robots' perceived Competence is negatively related to anthropomorphism.
Perceived Sociability, Morality, Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority vary with anthropomorphism.
Warmth dimension of the Stereotype Content Model is split into Sociability and Morality.
Findings give first insights on whether anthropomorphized robots may need different legal treatment.
annotation.summary_en: Two empirical studies using the Stereotype Content Model, split into Competence, Sociability and Morality, examine public perception of prosthesis users and robots of varying anthropomorphism. Study 2 also measures perceived Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority, giving first insights into whether anthropomorphic robots might require different legal treatment as workplace co-workers.
annotation.title_clean: Embodied Digital Technologies: First Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
annotation.title_en: Embodied Digital Technologies: First Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
